newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers contract must be concluded - Treu.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers contract must be concluded - Treu.

text.p: Italian metalworkers and employers must reach an accord on renewing a pay contract and the government's proposal for a monthly average rise of 200,000 lire ($129) could be flexible, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Thursday.
"This contract must be concluded," he told reporters attending a conference. "I've always said that our proposal is open to some flexibility."
Asked if he though it was possible to avoid a threatened general strike, he said: "It's always possible to avoid a strike as long as negotiations continue."
In a bid to break the long-running stalemate, the government last month proposed that workers should be given a 200,000 lire a month pay rise to cover the 1996-98 contract period.
Sergio Cofferati, leader of Italy's biggest trades union confederation, CGIL, said the government's proposal should be conclusive but that there was room for discussion on ways of applying it.
Also in Milan to attend a political meeting, he told reporters the government's proposal was "correct, in line with incomes policy and non-inflationary."
The Federmeccanica employers' association has rejected the proposal for a 200,000 lire pay hike as inflationary, so far refusing a rise of more than 139,000 lire a month.
Cofferati said, "Federmeccanica doesn't want to conclude the contract, they are hostile to the unions as well as the government."

He said a decision regarding a possible general strike in support of the metalworkers' demands would be considered by an executive committee meeting of the three major union federations, CGIL, CISL and UIL, on January 24.
Trades unions have already begun a series of factory-by-factory strike action to put pressure on employers.
Metalworkers held two-hour stoppages on Thursday at carmaker Fiat 's Mirafiori and Rivalta plants. Unions said participation was high but the company said it was low.
